Five verbs. Almost every table you will ever need is some arrangement of these.

| Verb | Does what | Changes |
|---|---|---|
| `filter()` | keeps rows that match a condition | fewer rows |
| `select()` | keeps columns you name | fewer columns |
| `mutate()` | adds or changes a column | more columns |
| `group_by()` | splits into groups | nothing visible |
| `summarise()` | collapses each group to one row | far fewer rows |

## The dataset

We use one small cohort throughout this page. Twelve people, followed up for a
cardiovascular event. Run this cell first; the later cells rebuild it for you
so you can run them in any order.

```{webr}
library(dplyr)

cohort <- tibble(
  id        = sprintf("P%02d", 1:12),
  district  = c("Kolar","Kolar","Kolar","Tumkur","Tumkur","Tumkur",
                "Hassan","Hassan","Hassan","Kolar","Tumkur","Hassan"),
  sex       = c("F","M","F","M","F","M","F","M","F","M","F","M"),
  age       = c(34, 51, 62, 45, 38, 71, 29, 55, 48, 66, 41, 59),
  smoker    = c(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE,
                FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE),
  years_fu  = c(5.0, 4.2, 5.0, 3.1, 5.0, 2.4, 5.0, 4.8, 5.0, 1.9, 5.0, 3.6),
  event     = c(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE,
                FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE)
)

cohort
```

`years_fu` is how long each person was followed. Note that it is shorter for
some people — they had the event, or they were lost. That column is what makes
this a real cohort rather than a spreadsheet, and Primer 6 is about it.

## `filter()` — keep rows

The condition goes inside. Note **`==`**, two equals signs, for "is equal to".
One equals sign is assignment and will not work here.

```{webr}
library(dplyr)
cohort <- tibble(
  id = sprintf("P%02d", 1:12),
  district = c("Kolar","Kolar","Kolar","Tumkur","Tumkur","Tumkur","Hassan","Hassan","Hassan","Kolar","Tumkur","Hassan"),
  sex = c("F","M","F","M","F","M","F","M","F","M","F","M"),
  age = c(34,51,62,45,38,71,29,55,48,66,41,59),
  smoker = c(FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE),
  years_fu = c(5.0,4.2,5.0,3.1,5.0,2.4,5.0,4.8,5.0,1.9,5.0,3.6),
  event = c(FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,FALSE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,FALSE)
)

cohort |> filter(district == "Kolar")
```

Several conditions, separated by commas, means **and**:

```{webr}
library(dplyr)
cohort <- tibble(
  id = sprintf("P%02d", 1:12),
  district = c("Kolar","Kolar","Kolar","Tumkur","Tumkur","Tumkur","Hassan","Hassan","Hassan","Kolar","Tumkur","Hassan"),
  sex = c("F","M","F","M","F","M","F","M","F","M","F","M"),
  age = c(34,51,62,45,38,71,29,55,48,66,41,59),
  smoker = c(FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE),
  years_fu = c(5.0,4.2,5.0,3.1,5.0,2.4,5.0,4.8,5.0,1.9,5.0,3.6),
  event = c(FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,FALSE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,FALSE)
)

cohort |> filter(smoker, age >= 50)
```

`smoker` on its own works because it is already `TRUE`/`FALSE`. Writing
`smoker == TRUE` is the same thing, more typing.

For **or**, use `|`. For "is it one of these", use `%in%`, which is much easier
to read than three `|`s:

```{webr}
library(dplyr)
cohort <- tibble(
  id = sprintf("P%02d", 1:12),
  district = c("Kolar","Kolar","Kolar","Tumkur","Tumkur","Tumkur","Hassan","Hassan","Hassan","Kolar","Tumkur","Hassan"),
  sex = c("F","M","F","M","F","M","F","M","F","M","F","M"),
  age = c(34,51,62,45,38,71,29,55,48,66,41,59),
  smoker = c(FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE),
  years_fu = c(5.0,4.2,5.0,3.1,5.0,2.4,5.0,4.8,5.0,1.9,5.0,3.6),
  event = c(FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,FALSE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,FALSE)
)

cohort |> filter(district %in% c("Kolar", "Hassan"))
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## `filter()` drops `NA` rows without telling you
If `age` is missing for someone, `age >= 50` is `NA`, not `TRUE`, so that row
disappears from both `filter(age >= 50)` and `filter(age < 50)`. Your two groups
then do not add up to your total, and nothing warns you. Count your rows before
and after every filter.
:::

## `select()` — keep columns

```{webr}
library(dplyr)
cohort <- tibble(
  id = sprintf("P%02d", 1:12),
  district = c("Kolar","Kolar","Kolar","Tumkur","Tumkur","Tumkur","Hassan","Hassan","Hassan","Kolar","Tumkur","Hassan"),
  sex = c("F","M","F","M","F","M","F","M","F","M","F","M"),
  age = c(34,51,62,45,38,71,29,55,48,66,41,59),
  smoker = c(FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE),
  years_fu = c(5.0,4.2,5.0,3.1,5.0,2.4,5.0,4.8,5.0,1.9,5.0,3.6),
  event = c(FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,FALSE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,FALSE)
)

cohort |> select(id, age, event)

# A minus sign drops instead
cohort |> select(-sex, -years_fu)
```

## `mutate()` — add a column

The new column is computed from existing ones, for every row at once.

```{webr}
library(dplyr)
cohort <- tibble(
  id = sprintf("P%02d", 1:12),
  district = c("Kolar","Kolar","Kolar","Tumkur","Tumkur","Tumkur","Hassan","Hassan","Hassan","Kolar","Tumkur","Hassan"),
  sex = c("F","M","F","M","F","M","F","M","F","M","F","M"),
  age = c(34,51,62,45,38,71,29,55,48,66,41,59),
  smoker = c(FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE),
  years_fu = c(5.0,4.2,5.0,3.1,5.0,2.4,5.0,4.8,5.0,1.9,5.0,3.6),
  event = c(FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,FALSE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,FALSE)
)

cohort |>
  mutate(age_group = if_else(age >= 50, "50+", "under 50")) |>
  select(id, age, age_group)
```

`if_else()` takes three things: the test, what to use when it is true, what to
use when it is false. For more than two categories, `case_when()` does the same
job with as many branches as you like:

```{webr}
library(dplyr)
cohort <- tibble(
  id = sprintf("P%02d", 1:12),
  age = c(34,51,62,45,38,71,29,55,48,66,41,59)
)

cohort |>
  mutate(age_band = case_when(
    age < 40            ~ "under 40",
    age < 60            ~ "40-59",
    .default            = "60+"
  )) |>
  select(id, age, age_band)
```

Read each line as "if this, then that". The first matching line wins, so order
matters: a 35-year-old is caught by the first line and never reaches the second.

## `group_by()` and `summarise()` — the pair that does the work

`group_by()` looks like it does nothing. `summarise()` then collapses each group
to a single row.

```{webr}
library(dplyr)
cohort <- tibble(
  district = c("Kolar","Kolar","Kolar","Tumkur","Tumkur","Tumkur","Hassan","Hassan","Hassan","Kolar","Tumkur","Hassan"),
  age = c(34,51,62,45,38,71,29,55,48,66,41,59),
  event = c(FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,FALSE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,FALSE)
)

cohort |>
  group_by(district) |>
  summarise(
    n         = n(),
    mean_age  = round(mean(age), 1),
    events    = sum(event),
    risk      = round(mean(event), 3)
  )
```

Look at `risk`. Because `event` is `TRUE`/`FALSE`, `sum()` counts the events and
`mean()` gives the proportion who had one. That proportion is the **risk** in
each district. That is a stratified analysis, in 4 lines.

`n()` counts rows in the group and takes no arguments. Include it in every
`summarise()` you write: a group mean over 3 people and one over 300 look
identical on the page unless you print the denominator.

## Putting it together

```{webr}
library(dplyr)
cohort <- tibble(
  id = sprintf("P%02d", 1:12),
  district = c("Kolar","Kolar","Kolar","Tumkur","Tumkur","Tumkur","Hassan","Hassan","Hassan","Kolar","Tumkur","Hassan"),
  sex = c("F","M","F","M","F","M","F","M","F","M","F","M"),
  age = c(34,51,62,45,38,71,29,55,48,66,41,59),
  smoker = c(FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE),
  years_fu = c(5.0,4.2,5.0,3.1,5.0,2.4,5.0,4.8,5.0,1.9,5.0,3.6),
  event = c(FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,FALSE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,FALSE)
)

cohort |>
  filter(age >= 40) |>
  group_by(smoker) |>
  summarise(
    n      = n(),
    events = sum(event),
    risk   = round(mean(event), 3)
  )
```

Two risks, one for smokers and one for non-smokers, among people aged 40 and
over. Divide one by the other and you have a risk ratio. That is Primer 7.

## Exercises

::: {.callout-note title="Exercise 1: filter and count"}
**Time:** 5 minutes

How many people in `cohort` are **smokers aged 50 or more**? Return a single
number.

```{webr}
#| setup: true
#| exercise:
#|   - ex_filter
#|   - ex_group
#|   - ex_rate
library(dplyr)

cohort <- tibble(
  id = sprintf("P%02d", 1:12),
  district = c("Kolar","Kolar","Kolar","Tumkur","Tumkur","Tumkur","Hassan","Hassan","Hassan","Kolar","Tumkur","Hassan"),
  sex = c("F","M","F","M","F","M","F","M","F","M","F","M"),
  age = c(34,51,62,45,38,71,29,55,48,66,41,59),
  smoker = c(FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE),
  years_fu = c(5.0,4.2,5.0,3.1,5.0,2.4,5.0,4.8,5.0,1.9,5.0,3.6),
  event = c(FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,FALSE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,TRUE,FALSE,FALSE)
)
```

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_filter
cohort |>
  filter(______) |>
  nrow()
```

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_filter
#| solution: true
cohort |>
  filter(smoker, age >= 50) |>
  nrow()
```

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_filter
#| check: true
# Smokers are P02(51), P04(45), P06(71), P08(55), P10(66), P12(59).
# Aged 50+: 51, 71, 55, 66, 59 = 5.  Aged >50 strictly: the same 5.
# Aged 50+ ignoring smoking: 51,62,71,55,66,59 = 6.
if (identical(as.numeric(.result), 5)) {
  list(correct = TRUE, message = "Correct — 5 smokers are aged 50 or over.")
} else if (identical(as.numeric(.result), 6)) {
  list(correct = FALSE, message = "That is everyone aged 50 or over, smoker or not. Add the smoker condition too, separated by a comma.")
} else if (identical(as.numeric(.result), 3)) {
  list(correct = FALSE, message = "That is everyone aged 60 or over. The threshold is 50, and you also need the smoker condition.")
} else if (identical(as.numeric(.result), 12)) {
  list(correct = FALSE, message = "Nothing was filtered out. Put both conditions inside filter().")
} else {
  list(correct = FALSE, message = "Two conditions inside one filter(), separated by a comma: smoker, and age >= 50.")
}
```

::: {.hint exercise="ex_filter"}
Commas inside `filter()` mean "and". `smoker` is already `TRUE`/`FALSE` so it
needs no comparison of its own.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Exercise 2: risk by sex"}
**Time:** 8 minutes

Produce a table with one row per `sex`, showing three columns: `n` (how many
people), `events` (how many had the event) and `risk` (the proportion who did,
rounded to 3 places).

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_group
cohort |>
  group_by(______) |>
  summarise(
    n      = ______,
    events = ______,
    risk   = ______
  )
```

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_group
#| solution: true
cohort |>
  group_by(sex) |>
  summarise(
    n      = n(),
    events = sum(event),
    risk   = round(mean(event), 3)
  )
```

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_group
#| check: true
# F: 6 people, 0 events, risk 0.  M: 6 people, 4 events, risk 0.667.
if (!is.data.frame(.result)) {
  list(correct = FALSE, message = "That is not a table. If there is a red error above, read that first. Otherwise start with cohort |> group_by(sex) |> summarise(...).")
} else if (nrow(.result) != 2) {
  list(correct = FALSE, message = sprintf("You got %d row(s); grouping by sex should give 2. Check what you passed to group_by().", nrow(.result)))
} else if (!all(c("n", "events", "risk") %in% names(.result))) {
  list(correct = FALSE, message = "The three columns must be named exactly n, events and risk.")
} else if (!isTRUE(all.equal(sort(as.numeric(.result$events)), c(0, 4)))) {
  list(correct = FALSE, message = "The event counts are wrong. sum(event) counts the TRUEs, because TRUE counts as 1.")
} else if (!isTRUE(all.equal(sort(as.numeric(.result$risk)), c(0, 0.667)))) {
  list(correct = FALSE, message = "The risks are wrong. Risk is mean(event), the proportion who had the event, rounded to 3 places.")
} else {
  list(correct = TRUE, message = "Correct. 0 of 6 women and 4 of 6 men, a risk of 0 and 0.667. Before you believe that difference, ask what else differs between the men and the women here — that question is Primer 9.")
}
```

::: {.hint exercise="ex_group"}
`n()` counts rows and takes no arguments. `sum(event)` counts the `TRUE`s.
`mean(event)` is the proportion, and you wrap it in `round(..., 3)`.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Exercise 3: a rate, not a risk"}
**Time:** 8 minutes

Risk ignores how long each person was followed. A **rate** does not: it divides
events by total person-time.

Compute the overall event rate per 100 person-years: total events divided by
total `years_fu`, times 100, rounded to 1 decimal place. Return a single number.

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_rate
______
```

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_rate
#| solution: true
round(sum(cohort$event) / sum(cohort$years_fu) * 100, 1)
```

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_rate
#| check: true
# 4 events over 50.0 person-years = 8.0 per 100 person-years.
if (isTRUE(all.equal(as.numeric(.result), 8))) {
  list(correct = TRUE, message = "Correct — 4 events in 50.0 person-years, so 8.0 per 100 person-years. Compare that with the risk, 4/12 = 0.333: same events, different denominator, different meaning.")
} else if (isTRUE(all.equal(as.numeric(.result), 33.3, tolerance = 1e-2))) {
  list(correct = FALSE, message = "You divided by the number of people, not by person-time. That is the risk as a percentage. A rate uses sum(years_fu) as the denominator.")
} else if (isTRUE(all.equal(as.numeric(.result), 0.1, tolerance = 1e-2))) {
  list(correct = FALSE, message = "You are close but have not multiplied by 100. The question asks per 100 person-years.")
} else if (is.numeric(.result) && length(.result) == 1) {
  list(correct = FALSE, message = "Right shape, wrong number. Total events divided by total years_fu, times 100, rounded to 1.")
} else {
  list(correct = FALSE, message = "You want one number: sum(cohort$event) / sum(cohort$years_fu) * 100, rounded to 1 place.")
}
```

::: {.hint exercise="ex_rate"}
`sum(cohort$event)` is the numerator. `sum(cohort$years_fu)` is the denominator.
Multiply by 100 and round.
:::
:::

## What you should now be able to do

- Keep rows with `filter()`, and remember that `NA` rows vanish from both sides.
- Keep or drop columns with `select()`.
- Add a computed column with `mutate()`, using `if_else()` or `case_when()`.
- Produce a grouped table with `group_by()` and `summarise()`, always including
  `n()`.
- Get a risk from `mean()` of a logical column, and a rate by dividing by
  person-time instead.
